fields.population: households in informal settlements aged 18-65 resident at least two years (survey); local officials, urban planners and NGO representatives (stakeholder survey)
fields.sample_size: 300 households (household survey) and 20 stakeholders (stakeholder survey); the methods section is written in the future tense ('will be conducted') and does not report a response rate, sampling frame or interview data
fields.effect_measure: descriptive percentages from a household survey and stakeholder survey, plus exploratory factor analysis (Varimax, five factors) and GIS/remote-sensing land-use change
fields.effect_estimate: Household survey (n = 300): frequent water supply interruptions 35%, unreliable electricity 28%, irregular or absent waste collection 55%, unsafe housing 23%, home ownership 45%, no green spaces 60%; 40% say population growth significantly affected service availability. Stakeholders (n = 20): 8 reported deteriorated water supply, 7 no change in sanitation; 7 judged urban-management policies insufficient and 5 'no' policies; barriers: lack of finance (6), lack of coordination (5), lack of urban planning (4); 3 proposed strengthening land-use regulations. Factor loadings are small for water and sewage access (about 0). Several tables do not reconcile with stated sample sizes (stakeholder tables sum to 14 or 19, not 20).
fields.model_type: descriptive survey statistics with exploratory factor analysis; GIS land-use change
fields.study_design: mixed-methods case study (household survey, stakeholder survey, spatial analysis); methods text describes planned rather than completed data collection
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: MMAT screening: S1=Yes, S2=Yes. Mixed-methods criteria (re-answered on the full text 2026-10-04): 5.1(rationale for mixed methods)=Yes (stated aim of a 'holistic view' combining spatial and socioeconomic data); 5.2(components effectively integrated)=No (household results, stakeholder results and GIS are presented separately); 5.3(outputs of integration interpreted)=No; 5.4(divergences addressed)=No; 5.5(components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition)=No (future-tense methods, no sampling or response detail, tables that do not reconcile with n, interview data not reported). Per MMAT's own guide, no composite score is computed -- 1 of 5 mixed-methods criteria met; concern high.
fields.section: Full text (IJSDP / IIETA web page): Introduction; Methodology 3.1-3.4; Results 4.1-4.2; Conclusion
fields.exact_location: 3.3 data collection and sampling; 4.1 household survey; 4.2 stakeholder survey; Tables 1-14

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a mixed-methods case study (300 households, 20 stakeholders) of unregulated urban sprawl in Al-Dora, Baghdad, read in full text 2026-10-04. Descriptive survey results on water interruptions and service deficits and stakeholder views that policies are insufficient. Methods are written as planned work, several tables do not reconcile with the sample sizes, and no regression is reported; MMAT 1 of 5 criteria met.
pdf_note: IIETA journal web page (about 74,000 characters), methods, results, Tables 1-14 and conclusion read; page numbers not available
notes: QUALITY: future-tense methods and non-reconciling tables (Tables 7 and 11 vs n = 20); MMAT 5.2-5.5 No. Legal content is thin (absence of legal frameworks asserted in the introduction; 3 of 20 stakeholders proposed stronger land-use regulation). Candidate for the weak-evidence list; eligibility (inclusion criterion on legal/administrative exposure) questionable. No effect-size row.
